feedback: Written before this candidate has raced. Geometry is held at the iteration 5 and 7 design, as the Builder asked. The evidence for holding is that span plus or minus 0.05 m cleared oval line loss in iteration 3 onward, while mass changes (0.7 to 0.6 kg in iteration 4) moved max_error by less than 0.002 m. Lowering base_speed to 1.2 (iteration 5) and raising kp to 2.8 with kd 0.25 at base_speed 1.1 (iteration 7) both left S-bend and slalom at 1 line-loss event each. So speed and a stronger gain have not cleared these losses. This candidate tests the opposite direction on gain: kp lowered to 2.2 and kd raised to 0.3, to see whether over-correction at bend onset is the cause. Decide the next geometry from the next race as follows. If S-bend and slalom line_loss_events are still 1 with geometry fixed, the loss is not geometric, so do not edit geometry; ask for the course position where the loss begins. If line_loss_events is 0 on all three tracks but max_error still approaches 0.06 m, widen wheel_track to 0.12 m. If runs complete but completion_time exceeds 2.5 s, test wheel_radius 0.035 m.
requested_changes: If line_loss_events is 0 on the oval, S-bend and slalom but max_error still approaches 0.06 m, set wheel_track to 0.12 m. Iterations 3 to 7 show body_width cannot move the 0.06 m off-track limit, so extra differential turn authority is the remaining bend lever.

If line_loss_events stays at 1 on the S-bend or slalom with the controller change, keep the geometry fixed and test sensor span x = +/-0.06 m (16 mm footprints, y = 0.04 m). This checks whether the outer sensors can still see tape at the limit of the off-track range, using evidence from iterations 3 to 7 where +/-0.05 m cleared the oval but not the bends.
Only if runs complete and completion_time exceeds 2.5 s, set wheel_radius to 0.035 m. Progress is 0.11 to 0.17 so far, so runs must first reach the finish before top speed matters.
